title: AH-1F / AH-1S Cobra (pilot)

sources.title: JoyPro cockpit catalog (panels, items and grip functions of the variant)

intro: The AH-1S and its final form, the AH-1F, are the single-engine Cobras of the US Army from the late 1970s, built to fight tanks with TOW missiles that the gunner guides. The modernised F has a head-up display for the pilot instead of the reflex sight and a rocket management system instead of the simple rocket pair selector. The grips and the round-dial instrument panel are taken as those of the AH-1G, so this guide builds on the AH-1G guide.

panels.name: Pilot head-up display
panels.text: The modernised AH-1F has a head-up display in place of the reflex sight: the glass screen in front of the pilot's eyes that shows aiming marks and flight numbers (HUD).
panels.context: The pilot aims the rockets and the stowed turret with its symbols while looking outside. JoyPro's sources do not describe its single switches.

controls.name: Combining glass
controls.text: The clear glass plate on which the aiming marks for the rockets and the gun appear, seemingly far out in front of the helicopter.
controls.context: The pilot lines the mark up with the target by pointing the helicopter.

controls.name: Brightness control
controls.text: This knob makes the symbols on the glass brighter or dimmer.
controls.context: The pilot sets it bright for sunlight and dim for night flying.

controls.name: Mode / test switch
controls.text: This switch chooses what the display shows and starts its self test.
controls.context: The test proves the display works before an attack. JoyPro's sources do not describe its single switches.

panels.name: Pilot armament panel (AH-1F)
panels.text: The pilot's master arm and the rocket management system of the modernised Cobra.
panels.context: The gunner aims the TOW missiles and the turret; the pilot fires the rockets with the settings made here.

controls.name: Master arm switch
controls.text: This is the main safety switch for the weapons (master arm): nothing fires while it is off.
controls.context: The pilot arms the weapons only when the helicopter is clear of friendly people and near the target, and makes them safe again before landing.

controls.name: Rocket management subsystem panel
controls.text: A small panel where the pilot chooses the rocket type, the fuze time (when the warhead goes off) and how many rockets leave with each press of the fire button.
controls.context: It replaced the simple pair selector of the AH-1G, because the F carries several kinds of rockets. JoyPro's sources do not describe its single switches.

controls.name: Wing stores emergency jettison
controls.text: A guarded switch that drops the wing stores in an emergency (jettison), to make the helicopter lighter. A cover over it has to be lifted first.
controls.context: It is used when the helicopter has an engine problem and must lose weight at once.

controls.name: TOW / turret status lights
controls.text: Lights that show what the gunner has selected, such as the TOW missiles, and whether the turret is stowed straight ahead.
controls.context: TOW is the wire-guided anti-tank missile the gunner guides with his sight; the lights keep the pilot informed.
